hints: Because the numerator and denominator have the same degree, the decomposition must include a constant term as well as two proper fractions.
Compare the coefficient of $x^2$ to determine $A$.
Substitute the roots of the two linear denominator factors to isolate $B$ and $C$, then check the identity.
walkthrough:
Because numerator and denominator have the same degree (2), perform polynomial division to find the polynomial quotient:
$$\dfrac{12x^2 + 4x - 1}{3x^2 - x - 2} = 4 + \dfrac{(12x^2 + 4x - 1) - 4(3x^2 - x - 2)}{3x^2 - x - 2}$$
$$4(3x^2 - x - 2) = 12x^2 - 4x - 8$$
$$\text{Remainder} = (12x^2 + 4x - 1) - (12x^2 - 4x - 8) = 8x + 7$$
$$f(x) = 4 + \dfrac{8x + 7}{(x - 1)(3x + 2)}$$

Decompose the remainder into partial fractions:
$$\dfrac{8x + 7}{(x - 1)(3x + 2)} = \dfrac{B}{x - 1} + \dfrac{C}{3x + 2}$$
$$8x + 7 = B(3x + 2) + C(x - 1)$$

Combine all terms to write $f(x)$ in partial fractions:
$$f(x) = 4 + \dfrac{3}{x - 1} - \dfrac{1}{3x + 2}$$

ai_rubric.Partial Fractions: Identifies $A+\frac{B}{x-1}+\frac{C}{3x+2}$; Identifies or derives $A=4$; Concludes with $f(x)=4+\frac{3}{x-1}-\frac{1}{3x+2}$.

hints: Start from the partial-fraction form found in part (i), expanding each proper fraction separately.
Rewrite $\frac{1}{x-1}$ as a multiple of $(1-x)^{-1}$ and $\frac{1}{3x+2}$ as a multiple of $(1+\tfrac32x)^{-1}$.
Use $(1+u)^{-1}=1-u+u^2+\cdots$ and retain terms only through $x^2$.
Include the constant polynomial term, then collect the constant, $x$, and $x^2$ coefficients.
walkthrough:
Rewrite each fraction in form suitable for binomial series expansion:
$$\dfrac{3}{x - 1} = -\dfrac{3}{1 - x} = -3(1 - x)^{-1}$$
$$-\dfrac{1}{3x + 2} = -\dfrac{1}{2\left(1 + \frac{3}{2}x\right)} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^{-1}$$

Expand $-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^{-1}$ using $(1 + u)^{-1} = 1 - u + u^2 - \dots$ with $u = \dfrac{3}{2}x$:
$$\left(1 + \dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^{-1} = 1 - \dfrac{3}{2}x + \left(\dfrac{3}{2}x\right)^2 = 1 - \dfrac{3}{2}x + \dfrac{9}{4}x^2$$
$$-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(1 - \dfrac{3}{2}x + \dfrac{9}{4}x^2\right) = -\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{4}x - \dfrac{9}{8}x^2$$

Sum the polynomial term 4 and the two expansions:
$$f(x) = 4 + (-3 - 3x - 3x^2) + \left(-\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{3}{4}x - \dfrac{9}{8}x^2\right)$$

State the final expansion up to $x^2$:
$$f(x) = \dfrac{1}{2} - \dfrac{9}{4}x - \dfrac{33}{8}x^2$$

ai_rubric.Binomial Expansion: Derives unsimplified expansions up to $x^2$ of each partial fraction. Add the value of $A$ to the sum. Concludes with $\frac12-\frac94x-\frac{33}{8}x^2$.
